source_user: Give one misleading intuition about decode and correct it. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Decode generates one or a few tokens per step and repeatedly reads model weights and KV state; it is often sensitive to memory bandwidth and scheduling.
corrected_answer: Misleading intuition: decode is always memory-bandwidth-bound, so increasing bandwidth must proportionally reduce latency. In reality, after prompt prefill each autoregressive step forms a new query, attends to the previously stored K/V, and appends the new position's K/V; this avoids rebuilding the prefix but still incurs kernel, launch, scheduling, and growing-cache costs. Boundary: short contexts, low concurrency, fused kernels, or compute/synchronization limits can dominate instead. Hold model, precision, runtime, batch policy, context/output lengths, and sampling fixed, then measure inter-token latency, throughput, memory traffic, utilization, and tail latency across loads before assigning causality.
risks: Bandwidth attribution without hardware counters can be false.
Prefill-inclusive latency can be mistaken for decode latency.
evidence_required: Matched repeated runs across context length and concurrency with separate prefill/decode timing, memory telemetry, utilization counters, and p50/p95/p99 latency.

source_user: Give one misleading intuition about decode and correct it. Case variant 2: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Decode generates one or a few tokens per step and repeatedly reads model weights and KV state; it is often sensitive to memory bandwidth and scheduling.
corrected_answer: Misleading intuition: decode recomputes the whole prompt on every generated token. With a supported KV cache, prefill computes the prefix once; each subsequent step uses the new token's query with cached prior keys and values, then appends the new K/V entries. Boundary: reuse is not automatic—token and positional compatibility, attention features, cache residency, and runtime support must hold; eviction or paging can force recomputation or add overhead. Compare cache-enabled and no-cache baselines with identical model, tokenizer, precision, workload, warm-up, and scheduler, and report cache hits, memory, failures, and latency percentiles.
risks: Unsupported prefixes or cache eviction invalidate the simple reuse story.
A no-cache baseline may differ in kernels and memory behavior.
evidence_required: Trace-verified cache construction/reuse and matched repeated measurements including output correctness, cache occupancy, recomputation, throughput, and tail latency.

source_user: Give one misleading intuition about decode and correct it. Case variant 3: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Decode generates one or a few tokens per step and repeatedly reads model weights and KV state; it is often sensitive to memory bandwidth and scheduling.
corrected_answer: Misleading intuition: because decode emits one token per iteration, its cost is independent of sequence length. The new query must access the accumulated K/V for the active prefix and the cache grows as tokens are generated, although implementation details such as paging, fusion, and grouped attention change the scaling. Boundary: the observed slope depends on context length, batch composition, cache layout, and hardware; do not extrapolate from one short prompt. Sweep prompt and output lengths at fixed model, precision, concurrency, and stopping policy, and measure per-token latency, memory use, and failure/OOM rate.
risks: Cache scaling differs across attention implementations.
Short-context results may hide capacity and paging effects.
evidence_required: A length-by-load matrix with cache-memory accounting, inter-token latency distributions, throughput, and OOM/eviction telemetry.

source_user: Give one misleading intuition about decode and correct it. Case variant 4: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Decode generates one or a few tokens per step and repeatedly reads model weights and KV state; it is often sensitive to memory bandwidth and scheduling.
corrected_answer: Misleading intuition: a higher aggregate decode tokens-per-second always means every request is faster. Batching lets a server share work across requests, but queueing, scheduler policy, and unequal sequence lengths can improve aggregate throughput while increasing individual latency. Mechanism: each request's decode step reads its prior K/V and appends a new K/V, while the runtime schedules many such steps together. Boundary: conclusions change with concurrency and batch limits, so aggregate throughput cannot substitute for per-request service metrics. Use the same arrival process and request mix, then report goodput, inter-token and end-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency, queue time, and failures.
risks: Aggregate throughput can conceal unacceptable tail latency.
Different arrival processes confound scheduler comparisons.
evidence_required: Load sweep with fixed request distributions, queueing telemetry, batch traces, per-request latency percentiles, throughput/goodput, and error counts.

source_user: Give one misleading intuition about decode and correct it. Case variant 5: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Decode generates one or a few tokens per step and repeatedly reads model weights and KV state; it is often sensitive to memory bandwidth and scheduling.
corrected_answer: Misleading intuition: a decode optimization is safe if it lowers latency, regardless of generated output. Decode is an autoregressive state update: the next-token distribution is computed from the current hidden state and cached K/V, then the chosen token changes the next step. Boundary: quantization, kernel changes, cache reuse bugs, or altered sampling can change output quality or correctness even when timing improves. Pin model weights, tokenizer, precision, decoding parameters, and stopping rules; verify deterministic or statistically equivalent outputs as appropriate, and jointly measure latency, throughput, memory, error rate, and quality on a representative workload.
risks: Latency-only evaluation can miss correctness or quality regressions.
Sampling differences can masquerade as model changes.
evidence_required: Golden-prompt output checks plus representative quality evaluation and matched performance measurements across lengths and load.

source_user: Design a small controlled experiment for decode. Case variant 1: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Decode generates one or a few tokens per step and repeatedly reads model weights and KV state; it is often sensitive to memory bandwidth and scheduling.
corrected_answer: Use one fixed model, tokenizer, hardware, precision, runtime, and decoding configuration. Generate a representative prompt set at two or more prefix lengths and output lengths, and compare a cache-enabled implementation with a correctly matched no-cache control. Warm up each condition, randomize trial order, repeat enough times for uncertainty, and hold concurrency and scheduler policy fixed. Mechanism: cached decode reuses prior K/V and computes/appends only the current position. Boundary: the no-cache comparison is not causal if kernels, batching, or memory allocation differ; also test cache capacity and a load level where eviction or paging may occur. Record prefill separately, inter-token and end-to-end latency, throughput, memory, cache hits/evictions, utilization, outputs, and failures.
risks: An unmatched control or unrepresentative prompt set can bias the result.
Capacity pressure may create nonlinear latency and failures.
evidence_required: Raw per-request traces, randomized repeated trials, confidence intervals, cache and memory telemetry, output equivalence checks, and OOM/error counts.

source_user: Design a small controlled experiment for decode. Case variant 2: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Decode generates one or a few tokens per step and repeatedly reads model weights and KV state; it is often sensitive to memory bandwidth and scheduling.
corrected_answer: Build a factorial microbenchmark varying context length and active concurrency while keeping model, precision, kernels, tokenizer, sampling, output length, and hardware fixed. Run cache-on and cache-off conditions with identical warm-up and batch policy, randomize order, and repeat each cell. Mechanism: after prefill, cache-on decode reads stored K/V for the new query and appends one position instead of rebuilding earlier positions. Boundary: cache-off may use a different execution path, and cache-on benefits may disappear when capacity causes eviction or paging, so trace both paths rather than infer reuse from timing. Report decode-only latency, TTFT separately, tokens/s, memory, queue time, cache events, utilization, confidence intervals, and errors.
risks: A single factor or low load can hide interactions.
Cache and no-cache implementations may not be comparable without path tracing.
evidence_required: Per-cell raw measurements with cache event traces, memory-pressure indicators, latency percentiles, and statistical uncertainty.

source_user: Design a small controlled experiment for decode. Case variant 3: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Decode generates one or a few tokens per step and repeatedly reads model weights and KV state; it is often sensitive to memory bandwidth and scheduling.
corrected_answer: Start with a fixed single-request baseline, then add controlled concurrency. Use prompts grouped by measured prefix length and a fixed generated-token budget, identical weights, precision, runtime, kernels, sampling, and stopping rules. Warm each condition, randomize trials, and repeat. The mechanism under test is incremental KV reuse: each new query attends to the prefix cache and only the new K/V is appended. Boundary: single-request behavior does not predict a batched server; scheduler, queueing, memory bandwidth, and cache capacity can change the bottleneck. Measure prefill and decode separately, inter-token latency, TTFT, throughput, memory/cache residency, utilization, queue time, outputs, and failures, with confidence intervals.
risks: Extrapolating from single-request results can misstate production behavior.
Fixed token budgets may not represent real stopping distributions.
evidence_required: Raw traces across concurrency and length cells, including scheduler decisions, cache residency, queueing, tail latency, and failure counts.

source_user: Design a small controlled experiment for decode. Case variant 4: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Decode generates one or a few tokens per step and repeatedly reads model weights and KV state; it is often sensitive to memory bandwidth and scheduling.
corrected_answer: Define a matched experiment with the same model graph, tokenizer, device, precision, runtime, prompt set, output-token budget, sampling, warm-up, and stopping rules. Vary only cache policy first, then separately vary context length and concurrency; randomize condition order and collect repeated trials. Mechanism: cache reuse supplies prior keys/values to the new-token query and appends the new position, avoiding prefix recomputation. Boundary: cache reuse requires an exact compatible prefix and sufficient residency; unsupported positional or attention features, eviction, or paging must be treated as separate conditions. Validate outputs, log cache hits/misses, and report prefill, decode, end-to-end latency percentiles, throughput, memory, utilization, and errors.
risks: Changing multiple factors together prevents causal attribution.
Cache compatibility failures may be hidden if only successful requests are timed.
evidence_required: Condition manifest, per-request traces, cache compatibility/hit logs, output checks, memory telemetry, and uncertainty including failed requests.

source_user: Design a small controlled experiment for decode. Case variant 5: include one concrete mechanism and one boundary condition.
source_assistant: Decode generates one or a few tokens per step and repeatedly reads model weights and KV state; it is often sensitive to memory bandwidth and scheduling.
corrected_answer: Use a fixed representative corpus of prompts with recorded lengths and a fixed maximum generated length. On identical hardware and software, compare two cache policies at several concurrency levels, keeping model, precision, tokenizer, decoding, scheduler, warm-up, and request arrival process constant. Randomize and repeat trials, and use bootstrap confidence intervals or another stated uncertainty method. Mechanism: cached autoregressive decode reads prior K/V for each new query and appends the current K/V, while a no-cache control rebuilds more prefix work. Boundary: do not claim a universal speedup if cache capacity, batching, paging, or request-length mix differs; report each operating point and failed/OOM requests. Capture TTFT separately from inter-token latency, throughput, queueing, memory, cache events, utilization, correctness, and output quality.
risks: Production-like arrival and length distributions may produce different results from synthetic fixed loads.
A cache policy speedup can trade against memory and tail latency.
evidence_required: Raw per-request results and bootstrap intervals over length/load cells, cache and memory traces, output validation, and complete error/OOM accounting.
